# Physiology, Muscarinic Receptor

**Authors:** Megan Kudlak, Prasanna Tadi

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Muscarinic receptors are G-coupled protein receptors involved in the parasympathetic nervous system. The only exception to these receptors is the sweat glands, which possess muscarinic receptors but are part of the sympathetic nervous system. They are named due to their increased sensitivity to muscarine, a component found in certain species of mushrooms. The molecule acetylcholine activates muscarinic receptors, allowing for a parasympathetic reaction in any organs and tissues where the receptor is expressed. Nicotinic receptors are ionotropic ligand-gated receptors that are also responsive to Ach, but they are mostly in the central nervous system. Muscarinic receptors are involved in peristalsis, micturition, bronchoconstriction, and several other parasympathetic reactions. Muscarinic receptors are a type of ligand-gated G-protein coupled receptor, functioning as either simulative regulative G-proteins (Gs) or inhibitory regulative G-proteins (Gi).  Ach stimulation of Gq to activate PLC and Ca2+. There are five different subtypes of receptors, that when either dysfunctional or overstimulated, can be targeted by several medications allowing for relief of symptoms.
